subject: Problem with changing posterior even when we set the prior SD to 0

messages.subject: Problem with changing posterior even when we set the prior SD to 0
parts:
Hi all! I was wondering if someone would be able to help me with a problem I am getting with INLA. Currently I am working with a spatio-temporal model, written with the following code. Just a couple notes about the model: the temporal component is defined by the "insptime" variable, and the second line of the code that defines datapred reflects that we only want predictions for the 4th insptime.

The problem is that in the code we use below, in the section that we have highlighted in red, we change the standard deviation of the prior of the model from prec = list(Intercept=0.1, not_sprayed=0.1)) to prec = list(Intercept=0.0, not_sprayed=0.0)), but when we look at the results of result$summary.fixed, the covariate and intercept of the model are still changing. We were wondering if anyone had any ideas about why they may be changing, even when we set the standard deviations of the priors to 0?

The code we used is below:

#===================================================================================
# IVb. Set up data in INLA format
#===================================================================================

# create datasets of observations 
dataforfit <- df[which(df$outcome == 1 | df$outcome == 0),]
datapred <- df[which(df$insptime == 4),]

# print out number of observations of each timestep
print(paste0("Number of observations from time step 1: ", length(which(dataforfit$insptime == 1))))
print(paste0("Number of observations from time step 2: ", length(which(dataforfit$insptime == 2))))
print(paste0("Number of observations from time step 3: ", length(which(dataforfit$insptime == 3))))
print(paste0("Number of observations from time step 4: ", length(which(dataforfit$insptime == 4))))

# print out sizes of dataforfit and datapred
print(paste0("Size of dataforfit: ", nrow(dataforfit)))
print(paste0("Size of datapred: ", nrow(datapred)))

# define time dimension
k <- length(unique(df$insptime))

# define two coordinate matrices
coords1<- cbind(dataforfit$LONGITUDEscale, dataforfit$LATITUDEscale)
coords <- cbind(datapred$LONGITUDEscale, datapred$LATITUDEscale)

# create mesh
mesh1 <- inla.mesh.2d(coords1, max.edge=c(50*S,50*S), cutoff=0.2)

# create two A matrices
A.est <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=mesh1,
                          loc=coords1,
                          group=dataforfit$insptime,n.group=k)

A.prd <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=mesh1, loc=coords, group=datapred$insptime)

# create SPDE object of Matern covariance matrix
spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh1, 
                          alpha=2,
                          theta.prior.mean=c(8,-5),
                          theta.prior.prec=c(0.1,0.1))

# create mesh index
mesh.index <- inla.spde.make.index(name='spatial', 
                                   n.spde=spde$n.spde,n.group=k)

# create stack object for data for fit
stack.est =
  inla.stack(data=list(y=dataforfit$outcome),
             A=list(A.est,1),
             effects=
               list(c(mesh.index,list(Intercept=1)),
                    list(
                      not_sprayed=dataforfit$not_sprayed)),
             tag="est")

# create stack object for data for prediction
stack.pred =
  inla.stack(data=list(y=datapred$outcome),
             A=list(A.prd,1),
             effects=
               list(c(mesh.index,list(Intercept=1)),
                    list(
                      not_sprayed=datapred$not_sprayed)),
             tag="pred")

# combine stack objects  
stack = inla.stack(stack.est, stack.pred)

# formula to input into INLA
formula <- y ~ -1 + Intercept + not_sprayed + f(spatial, 
                                                model=spde, 
                                                group=spatial.group, 
                                                control.group=list(model='ar1', 
                                                                   hyper=list(theta=list(prior='pccor1', param=c(0, 0.9)))))

#===================================================================================
# IVc. Run INLA model
#===================================================================================

# priors are set by control.fixed
result <- inla(formula,
               data = inla.stack.data(stack, spde=spde),
               family = c("binomial"),verbose=TRUE,
               #control.predictor = list(A=inla.stack.A(stack), compute=TRUE,link=1)  # Produces estimates
               control.predictor = list(A=inla.stack.A(stack), compute=TRUE,link=1, precision=.001)  # sets the precision on the A matrix low should speed things up!
               ,control.inla = list(reordering = "metis")
               ,control.fixed = list(mean = list(Intercept=-6.9, not_sprayed=1.17), # Prior means
                                     prec = list(Intercept=0.1, not_sprayed=0.1))  #Prior standard deviations
               #,num.threads=4  # uses 4 cores may be helpful
)

# runs a second inla model starting at the median of the first one
result <- inla.rerun(result)  

result.f <- inla.spde2.result(result, "spatial", spde, do.transf=TRUE)

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem with changing posterior even when we set the prior SD to 0
parts:
Hi Justin,
prec is not the standard deviation. It's the inverse of the variance (the precision). You need to make it large if you want the standard deviation to be almost zero.

Best wishes

Dan

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem with changing posterior even when we set the prior SD to 0
parts:
Also,
I'm pretty sure you don't want to mess with the control.predictor
"precision" parameters, since that is a numerical method tweaking
parameter, and not a proper model parameter.
(And setting that precision to a small value means that you decouple
your observations from the latent variables, so your estimates and
predictions will be meaningless...)

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem with changing posterior even when we set the prior SD to 0
parts: Thanks! By chance, would anyone have a guess as to why running this model twice (after taking out the control.predictor "precision" parameter as Finn mentioned) will give different results? Many thanks in advance.
On Thursday, February 22, 2018 at 3:00:00 PM UTC-5, Finn Lindgren wrote:

Also,
I'm pretty sure you don't want to mess with the control.predictor
"precision" parameters, since that is a numerical method tweaking
parameter, and not a proper model parameter.
(And setting that precision to a small value means that you decouple
your observations from the latent variables, so your estimates and
predictions will be meaningless...)

Finn

On 22 February 2018 at 19:53, Justin Sheen <justin...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thanks so much ! :-)
>
> On Thursday, February 22, 2018 at 2:42:54 PM UTC-5, Daniel Simpson wrote:
>>
>> Hi Justin,
>> prec is not the standard deviation. It's the inverse of the variance (the
>> precision). You need to make it large if you want the standard deviation to
>> be almost zero.
>>
>> Best wishes
>>
>> Dan
>>
